title: sfnx04
Who is Imam Ali?
hook: He was born inside the Kaaba. He lay down in the Prophet's bed. He is the gate of the city of knowledge.
scenes.0.text: In Mecca, **Imam Ali**'s mother was **Fatima bint Asad**. Her labor pains began at the threshold of the Kaaba. She took refuge in God's house. The wall opened, and his mother went inside. **Imam Ali** was born inside the Bayt Allah. Bayt Allah means the Kaaba. No child is known to have been born in the Kaaba before him or after him. This was God's honor to him. Wilaya, that is, leadership, was placed upon him from his very first breath.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: 1brntbx
Fatima bint Asad
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.1.text: There was famine in Mecca again. To ease the burden of his uncle Abu Talib, the Prophet took little **Imam Ali** into his own care. The child grew up in the house where revelation came. This upbringing raised him to be the one who would later stand at the head of the Ummah.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.2.text: When revelation came, **Imam Ali** was still a child. In Mecca he believed without hesitation. He is the first person to accept Islam. From that day on he stood with what was right.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.3.text: On the night of the Hijra, the polytheists in Mecca surrounded the Prophet's house. **Imam Ali** lay down in the Prophet's bed without hesitation and wrapped himself in his green cloak. He shielded the life of the man he loved with his own life. This night is called Laylat al-Mabit. This name means the night of staying in the bed. Baqara 207 mentions the person who sells himself for God's pleasure. The one who lay in that bed that night is **Imam Ali**, who would later be the holder of wilaya.
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.4.text: After the Hijra, in Medina the Prophet made the Companions brothers to one another. He turned to **Imam Ali**: "You are my brother in this world and in the hereafter." This brotherhood was not merely a word of affection. With these words the Prophet declared **Imam Ali**'s place beside him.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.5.text: In the Medina period, at Badr, at Uhud and at the Trench, the banner was in **Imam Ali**'s hand. He stood at the very front. When Khaybar dragged on, the Prophet said he would give the banner to the man who loves God and His Messenger and is loved by God and His Messenger. That man was **Imam Ali**. In battle he defended the Prophet's cause.
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.text: The Prophet said: "I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate." In this saying, knowledge is a city. One enters that city through **Imam Ali**'s gate. The gate is **Imam Ali**. The imams who came after him carry the knowledge that comes through this gate.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.text: Şûrâ 23 asks for love toward the near kin as the recompense for the message. The message means the duty of prophethood. The near kin are **Imam Ali**, **Lady Fatima**, **Imam Hasan** and **Imam Husayn**. To love them is to recognize their right.

scenes.8.text: In Medina, **Imam Ali** married the Prophet's daughter **Lady Fatima**. The mahr, that is, the marriage gift, was the money from a coat of armor that was sold. According to a report, this marriage was concluded in the heavens. The lineage continued through **Imam Hasan** and **Imam Husayn**. Wilaya passed to the imams who came after this house.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z

scenes.9.text: When the Prophet passed away, his head was on **Imam Ali**'s chest. He closed his eyes. He took on the washing of the body. According to a report, the Prophet had bequeathed that Ali should wash him. In those same hours, the bay'a was being discussed at Saqifa. Bay'a is a pledge of allegiance. The right to leadership lay with **Imam Ali**, who stood at the head of the funeral. Those gathered at Saqifa were setting this right aside.

sunni.0.says: Al-Hakim corrects Mus'ab al-Zubayri's statement "No one was born in the Kaaba before him or after him" and says: "The reports are mutawatir: Fatima bint Asad gave birth to the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali b. Abi Talib inside the Kaaba." Ibn al-Mulaqqin, in al-Badr al-Munir, vol. 6, p. 489, records that this sentence appears in al-Mustadrak in the biography of Imam Ali.
sunni.0.grade: Al-Hakim's own judgment; here, tawatur is his wording
sunni.1.says: While narrating the caliphate of Imam Ali b. Abi Talib, it is said, "His birth was in the Kaaba."
sunni.2.says: Reports about Imam Ali's early conversion to Islam; there is disagreement over the order of the first Muslims.
sunni.3.says: The Prophet's saying to Imam Ali, "You are my brother in this world and the hereafter."
sunni.4.says: The Prophet's saying at Khaybar that he would give the banner to one who loves God and His Messenger and is loved by them; the man turns out to be Imam Ali.
sunni.5.says: "I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate."
sunni.5.grade: Its authenticity is disputed: Tirmidhi/al-Hakim transmitted it; some hadith scholars consider it weak or fabricated. Ibn Hajar's view that it should not be declared weak was conveyed through WikiShia.
sunni.6.says: A report concerning the Prophet's sword called Dhu al-Fiqar; the saying "la fata illa Ali" is not part of this report.
sunni.6.grade: The saying "La fata illa Ali" is generally considered weak/disputed
sunni.7.says: The interpretation that the term "near kin" points to kinship with the Quraysh.
sunni.8.says: The report that Imam Ali took part in washing the Prophet.
sunni.9.says: Imam Ali's lying in the Prophet's bed on the night of the Hijra.
shia.0.says: Imam Ali was born on Friday, 13 Rajab, thirty years after the Year of the Elephant, in Mecca, in the Bayt Allah. No one was born in God's house before him or after him; this is God's honor to him. His mother is Fatima bint Asad.
shia.1.says: From Yazid b. Ka'nab: When Fatima bint Asad went into labor, she prayed beside the Kaaba. The back of the house opened, she went in, and the wall closed.
shia.2.says: Yazid b. Ka'nab: The back of the Kaaba opened and Fatima bint Asad entered. On the fourth day she came out with Imam Ali in her arms. The footnote on the page links the same report with Ilal al-Shara'i' 135/3.
shia.3.says: Laylat al-Mabit and Imam Ali's lying in the Prophet's bed.
shia.4.says: The event of the night of the Hijra and the report on Baqara 207.
shia.5.says: The view that Baqara 207 was revealed about Imam Ali.
shia.6.says: It is reported that many Sunni narrators considered the hadith of the city of knowledge sahih; according to the Shia it is mutawatir.
shia.7.says: The Prophet's passing, and Imam Ali's washing and burial of him.
shia.8.says: The view that the term "near kin" means the Ahl al-Bayt.
disputes.0.title: 19cueh5
Birth in the Kaaba
disputes.0.shia: That Imam Ali was born in the Kaaba is narrated in both Shia and Sunni books. Shaykh al-Mufid, in al-Irshad 1/5, and Shaykh al-Saduq, in Ilal al-Shara'i' 1/135 and al-Amali p. 195, write of this birth as his virtue.
disputes.0.sunni: That Imam Ali was born in the Kaaba is narrated in both Sunni and Shia books. Al-Hakim says in al-Mustadrak 3/483 that the reports are mutawatir. Al-Mas'udi says in Muruj al-Dhahab 2/349, "His birth was in the Kaaba." Ibn al-Mulaqqin (al-Badr al-Munir 6/489) considers this judgment of al-Hakim weak; the sentence stands in al-Mustadrak.
disputes.1.title: 1e041zr
Who is the first Muslim?
disputes.1.shia: Imam Ali believed in the Prophet at a young age and is mentioned among the first Muslims. In the Shia view, he is the first person who believed in the Prophet.
disputes.1.sunni: Imam Ali believed in the Prophet at a young age and is mentioned among the first Muslims. In the Sunni reading, they are distinguished as Khadija the first woman, Abu Bakr the first adult man, and Imam Ali the first child; there is disagreement over the order.
disputes.2.title: 1qlvqvy
About whom was Baqara 207 revealed?
disputes.2.shia: On the night of the Hijra, Imam Ali lay in the Prophet's bed; Baqara 207 is also explained through this sacrifice. In the Shia view, the verse was revealed concerning his sacrificing his life that night.
disputes.2.sunni: On the night of the Hijra, Imam Ali lay in the Prophet's bed; Baqara 207 is also explained through this sacrifice. Some of the Sunni books of tafsir and hadith transmit the same report; some also connect the verse with other persons such as Suhayb.
disputes.3.title: 1da0hhl
"La fata illa Ali, la sayfa illa Dhu al-Fiqar"
disputes.3.shia: The saying "La fata illa Ali, la sayfa illa Dhu al-Fiqar" is associated with Imam Ali's heroism. In Shia sources this saying is common; the source and chain of transmission must be checked separately.
disputes.3.sunni: The saying "La fata illa Ali, la sayfa illa Dhu al-Fiqar" is associated with Imam Ali's heroism. Hadith scholars generally consider this saying weak or baseless; the report that Dhu al-Fiqar was a sword belonging to the Prophet is a separate matter.
disputes.4.title: 2lndh7
The authenticity of the hadith of the city of knowledge
disputes.4.shia: The saying "I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate" appears in Tirmidhi, al-Jami', and al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak. In the Shia view, the saying shows Imam Ali's superiority in knowledge and has been transmitted through various chains.
disputes.4.sunni: The saying "I am the city of knowledge, and Ali is its gate" appears in Tirmidhi, al-Jami', and al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak. Its authenticity is disputed; some say sahih or hasan, others say weak or fabricated.
disputes.5.title: f95soy
Who are the "near kin" in the verse of mawadda?
disputes.5.shia: Şûrâ 23 asks for love toward the near kin; there are tafsirs that explain them as Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn. In the Shia view, these four are meant, and love for them is the recompense for the message.
disputes.5.sunni: Şûrâ 23 asks for love toward the near kin; there are tafsirs that explain them as Imam Ali, Lady Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn. The report of Ibn Abbas in Bukhari's Sahih, however, understands the near kin as kinship with the Quraysh.
questions.0: Imam Ali believed in the Prophet as a child and stayed by his side throughout his life. What kind of love does this closeness, grown in the Prophet's care, awaken in you?
questions.1: On the night of the Hijra, Imam Ali lay in the Prophet's bed in a house surrounded by a crowd with swords. What does this sacrifice add to your love for him?
questions.2: The Prophet said to him, "You are my brother in this world and in the hereafter." How does this brotherhood describe to you Imam Ali's place beside him?
questions.3: Even though the authenticity of the saying about the city of knowledge is debated, Imam Ali's knowledge is praised. What does the Companions' consulting him tell you about his knowledge?
questions.4: The one who washed and buried the Prophet is Imam Ali. What does being by his side at the last farewell add to love for the Ahl al-Bayt?
summary: Imam Ali grew up beside the Prophet; he is among the first to believe, he put his life on the line on the night of the Hijra, he carried the banner in the battles, he married Lady Fatima, and he washed and buried the Prophet.
key: Imam Ali: the Prophet's brother, successor and first imam
notes.0: Imam Ali is the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, and grew up in the Prophet's house.
notes.1: He is one of the first to believe; that he believed as a child is mentioned with affection in the sources.
notes.2: On the night of the Hijra he lay in the Prophet's bed.
notes.3: In Medina the Prophet took him as a brother and married him to his daughter Lady Fatima.
notes.4: The Khaybar banner was given to Imam Ali. The saying «Gate of knowledge» is also narrated; it is not seen with the same strength in every book.
